text:
elaine: hitting a weird one during hack week onboarding. Installed redwoodctl via the org brew formula, ran `redwoodctl login` (browser flow succeeded) but localserve started up as the helper user and kept showing "not authenticated".

elaine: looks like localserve can't read my token file even though it's in ~/.config/redwood/auth.cache. Anyone seen service vs user file-perms mismatch?

tom: which user does localserve run as in your setup? system service or launchctl per-user?

elaine: our dev image runs localserve under a dedicated user 'redwood-service' (non-root) to isolate sockets. I installed with my normal account; umask on the image is 027.

ricardo: ahhh umask 027 will create files with perms 750/640 depending. If the token file is 0600 the service user can't read it, so CLI can renew but the service can't. That would explain the mismatch and the repeated auth prompt from the service side.

elaine: verified: `stat -f '%OLp %Su %Sg %N' ~/.config/redwood/auth.cache` -> `-rw------- ela ine staff /Users/elaine/.config/redwood/auth.cache` (so service can't read).

tom: quick workaround: `chmod 640 ~/.config/redwood/auth.cache && chgrp redwood-service ~/.config/redwood/auth.cache` and restart localserve. But that's a pain for onboarding.

elaine: did that and service now sees me. But we shouldn't rely on manual fixes.

ricardo: agree. Two follow-ups: (1) installer/postinstall should set explicit perms and group on created config files (e.g., 0640 + group redwood-service when system manages a helper), or at least make them world-readable for dev images, (2) redwoodctl/localserve should detect unreadable config and print a clearer diagnostics message (`cannot read token file at X — check umask/install perms or run 'redwoodctl doctor'`) instead of silently falling back to unauthenticated behavior.

elaine: also saw this in CI images where Dockerfile sets `USER developer` after a root install; the files end up owned by root with restrictive perms. Might be two different root causes (ownership vs umask).

ci-bot: Created job log snippet: `./build-image.sh -> brew install redwoodctl --formula -> umask 027 -> files created 0600` (artifact attached to job 5123).

devex-bot: Created issue #4987: "installer: ensure config files created with explicit perms and optional group for helper services; add unreadable-config diagnostic". Labels: devex, infra, high-priority.

tom: action items: (A) update homebrew formula postinstall to call `install --mode=0640` or `umask` normalization, (B) add a `redwoodctl doctor` check for unreadable/owner-mismatch config and clearer error text, (C) add a note in quickstart for environments that change umask or install as root.

elaine: I'll paste the minimal Dockerfile repro to the issue and test the fix if someone wants to review. Marking my onboarding snag resolved for now.

ricardo: thanks — this would have tripped a few internal dev images. I'll take the formula change.
